message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *Note: Released in theaters in 2017 but had a wide streaming release in 2020.* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A fresh take on the classic horror‑thriller formula, blending psychological suspense with social commentary on domestic abuse. |
| 2 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller, capturing the tension of the 1969 trial with sharp dialogue and strong ensemble performances. |
| 3 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish film that uses a tense narrative to explore themes of paranoia and mob mentality, delivering a chilling critique of modern society. |
| 4 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though released in 2019, its extended theatrical run in 2020 made it a prominent crime epic, featuring Scorsese’s signature storytelling and a stellar cast. |
| 5 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily Sullivan, David Wenham | A historical crime‑drama set in colonial Australia, known for its visceral storytelling and strong female lead. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval crime‑thriller that examines power dynamics and justice, praised for its cinematography and complex characters. |
| 7 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A gritty procedural that blends mystery with character study, noted for its atmospheric tension and strong performances. |
| 8 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | A stylish gangster comedy‑thriller that balances humor with a fast‑paced plot, celebrated for its witty script and ensemble cast. |
| 9 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish sci‑fi allegory that doubles as a social thriller, lauded for its stark visuals and thought‑provoking premise. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** (2020) – *Note: This is a remake of the 1933 classic.* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern retelling that reimagines the story as a psychological thriller about gaslighting and abuse, praised for its suspenseful pacing and strong lead performance. |

These titles represent a mix of mainstream blockbusters, indie gems, and international releases that were either released directly to streaming platforms or had limited theatrical runs in 2020. Each offers a distinct take on the crime‑thriller genre, from psychological horror to courtroom drama to historical intrigue.
